images.title: 1-3 Place Saint-Michel
images.author: Beyond My Ken (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Corner block: 45-degree mansard comble with round dormers, bossage-rusticated ground-floor arcades, continuous balcon filant with sculpted balustrade at 2nd floor and plain ironwork balcon filant at top (5th/6th) floor, strict cornice-line unity across the block.

images.title: 1-7 Place Saint-Michel
images.author: Beyond My Ken (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Two adjacent Second Empire buildings sharing identical cornice, mansard-roof, and balcon-filant lines across the parcel boundary -- clean evidence of strict block unity.

images.title: 5-7 Place Saint-Michel
images.author: Beyond My Ken (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Comble with round dormers and balcon filant at 2nd floor; a street tree obscures much of the ground-floor bossage and shopfronts.

images.title: Avenue de l'Opéra enfilade
images.author: besopha (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Long raking street view showing the enforced block unity of the avenue: matching cornice height, mansard roofline, and balcon-filant bands repeating unbroken across many separate buildings. Oblique/receding angle rather than frontal.

images.title: Avenue de l'Opéra no. 38
images.author: Freepenguin (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Near-frontal full facade: sculpted balcon filant with scrollwork balustrade at 2nd floor, plainer continuous balcon filant at top floor just under the comble, dormers with round pediments, giving a clean read of the two-balcon-band rule.

images.title: 50 Boulevard Magenta, caryatid detail
images.author: FLLL (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Close detail of a sculpted caryatid (by Charles Gauthier) supporting the 2nd-floor balcon filant, with the wrought-iron balustrade of the floor above visible -- clean evidence of the ornamental treatment at the balcon-filant floor.

images.title: 56 Boulevard Magenta, atlas figures
images.author: FLLL (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Close detail of paired sculpted atlas figures (by Sébastien Delarue) framing a window below a continuous ironwork balcon filant -- dated facade (1866-1867), squarely inside the canonical Second Empire window.

images.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol corner
images.author: Thierry Bezecourt (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Corner building on one of Haussmann's first pierced boulevards: mansard comble, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor and dormer-level balustrade at top floor, ground-floor shopfronts under a rusticated base.

images.title: Haussmannian building with corner dome
images.author: Dale Cruse (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
images.street: Paris (exact address not recorded on Commons)
images.shows: Corner pavilion with a domed roof and a row of near-identical Haussmannian buildings receding down the block, each with matching balcon-filant bands -- good block-unity evidence, oblique/receding framing.

images.title: 105 & 107 Rue de Rennes
images.author: Fred Romero (Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Near-frontal facade with full-height sculpted caryatids flanking the ground-floor shopfronts, a decorated balcon filant at 2nd floor immediately above them, and a plainer continuous balcon filant at the top floor below the comble.

images.title: Rue Halévy dormers and comble detail
images.author: Vania Teofilo (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Close, upward-angled detail of the mansard comble: a run of pedimented dormer windows above a continuous wrought-iron balcon filant and Corinthian-capped pilasters -- clean evidence of the roof/comble geometry and top-floor balcony band.

images.title: 12 Rue Halévy
images.author: Tangopaso (Wikimedia Commons)
images.shows: Full, near-frontal corner facade: rusticated bossage ground floor with round-arched openings, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor, plain ironwork balcon filant at top floor just under the mansard comble -- one of the cleanest single-image reads of the whole family's defining stack.

notes: All images from Wikimedia Commons, downloaded at the ~1280px thumbnail size returned by the API (iiurlwidth=1000 bucket), not full-resolution originals. Selection favours canonical, well-attested Haussmannian boulevard buildings (Place Saint-Michel, Avenue de l'Opéra, Boulevard Magenta, Rue Halévy, Rue de Rennes, Boulevard de Sébastopol) that clearly show the 45-degree mansard comble, rusticated bossage socle, and the two-band balcon filant (2nd floor + top floor) that defines this family. Several strong Commons candidates tagged 'Haussmannian' were rejected as out-of-period for this canonical 1853-1870 family: one facade carries an architect's plaque dated 1892, others show Art Nouveau/eclectic bow-windows, mosaic tile insets, or ornate Beaux-Arts corner domes typical of the 1880s-1900s rather than the strict Second Empire idiom. An aerial/bird's-eye Commons photo and a tourist-bus-obstructed shot were also dropped per the selection criteria. Exact construction dates were only available in the source description for one image (56 Boulevard Magenta, 1866-1867); all other images have year left blank rather than guessed, per instructions. 'klass' reflects the apparent socioeconomic register of the building fabric shown (mostly grand boulevard-front buildings with sculpted ornament), not a claim about construction date.
